title: Stump Grinding vs. Full Stump Removal: What's the Difference?
meta_title: Stump Grinding vs. Full Stump Removal
meta_description: Grinding and full removal solve the same visible problem in different ways. Here's what actually separates the two approaches to an old stump.
lede: Getting rid of a stump can mean two pretty different things depending on which approach is used.
excerpt: What separates stump grinding from digging out a stump entirely.

sections.heading: Grinding Works From the Top Down
paragraphs: Grinding breaks the stump down mechanically from the top, going at least 6 inches below grade, without pulling the root system out of the ground. What's left is a hole filled with wood debris rather than an open excavation.

sections.heading: Full Removal Digs the Whole Thing Out
paragraphs: Full removal involves excavating the stump and much of its root system out of the ground entirely, which leaves a larger disturbed area and generally more ground to restore afterward.

sections.heading: Why Grinding Is the More Common Approach
paragraphs: For most residential and commercial situations, grinding solves the practical problems, a trip hazard, a mower obstacle, an eyesore, without the larger disturbance that full excavation involves. Raised roots nearby can still be addressed as part of a grinding job.

sections.heading: What Restoration Looks Like After Each
paragraphs: After grinding, topsoil backfill over the ground area is usually enough to prep it for grass. After full removal, the larger excavated area typically needs more substantial fill and grading before it matches the surrounding yard.

faqs.q: Does grinding remove the roots too?
faqs.a: Grinding addresses the stump and, when needed, nearby raised roots, but it doesn't excavate the full root system the way full removal does.
Grinding generally leaves a smaller, more contained area to deal with than full excavation, which disturbs more ground.

faqs.q: Which one is more common for a typical yard?
faqs.a: Grinding is the more common approach for most residential and commercial situations, since it solves the practical problems without a larger excavation.
